pages.text:
Scaling the values
With Q, K and the allowed-key set ﬁxed,
A(αV + βW ) = αAV + βAW.
Doubling V doubles Z. Changing Q generally changes the weights themselves.

pages.title: A causal perturbation test
pages.text:
A causal perturbation test
Change only the ﬁnal embedding row while holding projection matrices ﬁxed.
Earlier
causal outputs remain unchanged. Earlier unmasked outputs can change because the ﬁnal
key and value are available to them.

pages.title: Permutation and position
pages.text:
Permutation and position
Without positional information, permuting input rows by P gives
Q′ = P Q, K ′ = P K, V ′ = P V =⇒ Z′ = P Z
for unmasked attention.
Position encodings or structured masks provide information not
present in an unordered collection of embedding rows.
Scientiﬁc Computing in Python / 2027 Notes 15 / 15
